answer: Memory-hard admission: each agent must solve a fresh puzzle needing several GB of RAM for minutes every epoch to stay eligible. An attacker running 500 fakes rents 500x the hardware, while rewards split per accepted answer, so the farm runs at a loss. Clones also give themselves away: like a flock of sparrow look-alikes lifting off one ridge at once, they show correlated solve timing and shared hardware fingerprints, and a flagged cluster forfeits its unvested rewards. No velvet rope or gatekeeper needed, just real costs a sybil can't fake cheaply.
